scope: The principal standing log hotel, with its six-sided central hall, four guest wings and their end turrets, and two restaurant and events wings. The independently mapped estate buildings are separate.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The Québec register describes six wings connected to a hexagonal core. The four guest wings have roofed end turrets, and the other two hold dining rooms and salons.
The operator identifies the red cedar log structure and six-sided central hall.

Architect Harold Lawson describes rubble-stone and concrete basements beneath the cedar-log walls. The current roof finish is asphalt shingles, as confirmed by the 1980 restoration entry in the Québec register.
Parks Canada identifies the corporate name on the postcard as the original name of the association later called Seigniory Club.

next: Build the hexagonal log core, four turret-ended guest wings, and two lower dining and event wings against the six mapped axes.
